chapter: Opinions on playing and old New Orleans
title: Why Foster avoids bass solos and prefers rhythm
summary: Bass solos lack foundation; Foster plays running chords and says dancers follow rhythm.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Some people told me they thought the tuba was a little bit too heavy of tone. Maybe it didn't swing like the string bass is...

You can't swing, see? You see, because guys are on tubas. I hear them all the time trying to take solos on tubas. They don't sound like nothing to me because nothing, something ain't there. It's a bass instrument. And why? It should be played as a bass, it's like a bass violin, see? They're ringing about solos. These guys taking their solos, see? The solos I take is not exactly the solos, it's running chords. That's right. Yeah.

See? There's no... I'm not... I'm in the melody and I'm not with the melody. I'm carrying the melody. I'm carrying the straight chords to the melody of that song. Now you can sing, if you know the number, you can sing the changes that I'm making. See? These guys take the solos and they're... Well, there's nothing happening. There's no foundation behind that. See? And I don't care for it, but I don't tell the other guy, I say it's great.
See? I never say it's great.

So people tell me, how do you like it? I say I don't like playing solos. Which I don't. I like that this time I play rhythm behind the other guy that ain't blowing. And if you play that correct rhythm behind the guy that's blowing, you get much credit as the man playing that melody. See? Because we're just like when we went to Rose in the Bar Room. We didn't have much of a band. I say they ain't got no band, but they sure it's got some good rhythm. I say I'll meet Paul Boblin. That was a great... And a guy, he's dead now, Bill Johnson, who gets our players from... He's from Ohio. And Lou Russell. He said they ain't got no band, but they got rhythm. Those people dance by rhythm. Yeah. See? See? No solo. I got a number that I'm going to play with. I made Joyce of Light and you heard that name.
Oh sure. That's a great thing.
